summary: Client message pages (GET /v1/client/messages, the phone's list) and the other mail lists that read graph claims (the message list, the unread mailbox summary, the mail backlog and its cleanup, GitHub watch closes) now include the stream items a member's messages shard holds, after the graph's mail; members advertise messages_stream_selectors=1 (db break-up step 4c-2a-2). Nothing in the product writes stream mail yet, so this changes nothing a user sees until a later release routes mail to the stream.

replay.detail: No claim is written or projected differently. A stream item's selector header is folded from the member-local stream mirror, and a subject the graph also holds is listed once, from the graph.

schema.detail: Two new triggers on the stream mirror's member-local tables (local_stream_sent_client_selector, local_stream_lifecycle_client_selector) queue a stream item's header in local_client_message_selectors_v1. Two more on that table (client_selector_stream_header_retired, client_selector_stream_header_deleted) and those two remove a meta key, client_message_selectors_v1_stream_headers_whole, whenever a stream item is queued or a stream header goes, under any build. This build puts the key back once its fold has caught up. A start that finds it missing runs a re-seed, which a second meta key (client_message_selectors_v1_stream_seed) tracks. A stream header's created_index is the stream base (2^48) plus its shard index. No new table, no user_version change, no change to any replicated table.

rules.detail: No admission rule changes. Lifecycle steps the mail backlog cleanup and GitHub watch closes take on a stream item are recorded in the shard as this member's steps, as conversations archive already records them, instead of being refused as claims for an unknown message.

compatibility.detail: Additive. A client page cursor gains an optional before_stream_index, the stream frontier its first page saw, so a continuation lists no stream item mirrored after it; cursors are issued and checked by the same member, and one without the field reads the current frontier. The daemon.started feature messages_stream_selectors=1 is informational: nothing routes on it. A member of a release without it (v0.3.28 and earlier) lists only graph mail.

downtime.detail: No migration. An upgraded member whose selectors are published queues stream headers through the mirror's triggers. Its first start, and any start after a build without stream headers ran, also runs a re-seed, which the maintenance worker does after start in pages of 64. A start after this build ran reads no mirror row; a member building its selectors for the first time reads the mirror in its backfill.

recovery.detail: Rolling back to a release without stream selectors leaves the stream headers in place, and a release with the stream mirror but not these selectors drops the header of a stream item it closes or newly mirrors. That build's own run of these triggers removes the whole-headers key. So, upgraded again, the first start re-seeds a header for every mirrored stream item that has none. A backup carries no selectors; the restored member rebuilds them, stream items included, from the restored graph and mirror.
